interest: Shows 1930 Japanese goodwill envoys thanking Americans for 1923 earthquake relief, with elite ties and heavy U.S. coordination.
overview: This file (Department of State decimal file 894.48B, File 592) comprises State Department "List of Papers" (docket and purport sheets) documenting official communications and diplomatic activities regarding the aftermath of the catastrophic 1923 Tokyo and Yokohama earthquake. Spanning entries from 1930 to 1936, the file consists of two primary segments: a general list of papers concerning the completed reconstruction of Tokyo, memorial services for disaster victims, and requests to publish 1923 earthquake correspondence in Foreign Relations of the United States (FRUS); and a four-page docket list (Jacket Cases 1 through 4) detailing the spring 1930 goodwill mission to the United States of the "People's Envoys of Gratitude," four young Japanese women sent by the Tokyo newspaper Jiji Shimpo to convey national appreciation for American disaster relief. The docket indexes diplomatic arrangements, customs and immigration clearances, itineraries, and official meetings with President Herbert Hoover, First Lady Lou Henry Hoover, former President Calvin Coolidge, and American Red Cross Chairman John Barton Payne, as well as formal letters of gratitude presented by Japanese civic and governmental leaders.
